title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is §5 of Grothendieck's notes on 'déploiement des espaces stratifiés'. The page passes from conic or cylindrical neighbourhoods, which are actual structures, to their germs. That move is what is needed to state a clean equivalence of categories, done on the next page, between a stratified space near a stratum and its 'unfolded' (déployé) version.

(1) Setting. Y ⊂ X, and T, T' are conic neighbourhoods of Y in X. Such a neighbourhood carries a cone parameter t ∈ [0,1[ with Y = {t = 0}. For λ ∈ ]0,1[, λT is the shrunken neighbourhood {t < λ} with its induced, rescaled conic structure.

(2) Equivalence of neighbourhoods. T ~ T' if there are λ, λ' with λT = λ'T' as conic structures over Y. The marginal addition notes that then ελT = ελ'T' for every ε ∈ ]0,1[. This gives transitivity: from λT = λ'T' and μT' = μ'T'' one gets λμT = λ'μT' = λ'μ'T''. A germ of conic neighbourhood is an equivalence class.

(3) Compatibility with a germ. A subspace X_i is compatible with a germ represented by T if it is compatible with λT for some λ. It is then compatible with every smaller λ'T, so the notion does not depend on the representative. The same holds for strict compatibility.

(4) Cylindrical germs. Being cylindrical (a collar Y × [0,1[) is invariant under the equivalence. So one gets germs of cylindrical neighbourhoods. These exist only when Y is a 'bord' (collared boundary) of X, as the parenthesis and the margin say.

(5) Key construction. Start from a pair (X̃*, Ẋ) with Ẋ closed in X̃* and equipped with a germ of cylindrical (collar) neighbourhoods, and a continuous map f: Ẋ → Y. Then X = X̃* ⊔_Ẋ Y, the pushout that collapses the boundary onto Y along f, contains Y. It inherits a germ of conic neighbourhoods: the collar becomes a mapping-cylinder neighbourhood. This conic germ is (probably) 'isotrivial', i.e. locally trivial, iff f is a fibration or fibre bundle.

The next page states the inverse statement as an equivalence of categories. On one side are systems (X̃*, Ẋ, cylindrical germ, Y, f); on the other are pairs (X, Y closed) with a conic germ τ. Unfolding a stratum is thus an equivalence: conic germ ↔ collar + attaching map, i.e. a blow-up or unzipping of the stratum.
errors: No real error. The definition of equivalence needs the marginal ε-remark to be transitive, and Grothendieck added exactly that.
The 'λT' notation is used for both conic and cylindrical neighbourhoods without saying how it is defined. For cylindrical germs it must mean truncation of the collar.

The final 'iff fibrant' claim is unproved and its meaning depends on the reading: locally trivial bundle versus Hurewicz or homotopy fibration. With the homotopy reading the statement would rather match a Quinn-style homotopy-link condition. With the bundle reading it matches local conic triviality.

ideas.what: Germs of conic/cylindrical neighbourhoods of a subspace, via equivalence under rescaling of the cone parameter; compatibility of strata with germs
ideas.modern_name: germs of tubular/conic neighbourhoods; germs of control data
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom, Mather (control data, 1970); Siebenmann (locally conelike spaces, 1972)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 discusses tame stratified structures and tubular neighbourhoods only informally

ideas.what: Recovering X from the boundary-with-collar X̃* plus an attaching map Ẋ → Y via the pushout X̃* ⊔_Ẋ Y; the conic germ is the mapping-cylinder neighbourhood
ideas.modern_name: mapping cylinder neighbourhoods; unfolding/blow-up of a stratum (unzipping)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quinn (homotopically stratified sets, 1988) for mapping cylinders; Verona (1984) and Brasselet–Hector–Saralegi (1991) for 'dépliement'; Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (2017) for 'unzipping'
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme alludes to dévissage of stratified spaces, but not this construction explicitly

ideas.what: The conic germ is isotrivial (locally trivial) iff the attaching map is a fibration
ideas.modern_name: local triviality of the link bundle; Thom isotopy lemma type statement

missed.claim: This page and the next state, in 1981–82, a categorical equivalence between spaces with a conic germ along a closed stratum and data (boundary space with collar germ, attaching map). This is essentially the 'unzipping'/resolution equivalence later formalised by Ayala–Francis–Tanaka for conically smooth stratified spaces, and the 'dépliement' of Brasselet–Hector–Saralegi. Grothendieck's purely topological, germ-based formulation is not credited in that literature.
missed.quote: alors $X = \tilde{X}^* \amalg_{\dot T} Y \supset Y$ est muni d'un germe de voisinages côniques
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is an early, explicit categorical formulation of unfolding stratified spaces. This is relevant to the history of the tame-topology programme in the Esquisse and to modern ∞-categorical stratified homotopy theory.

deep.surprise_reason: The page itself consists of routine germ definitions plus the mapping-cylinder construction. Its interest is as the setup for the next page's equivalence of categories. That equivalence anticipates later 'unfolding/unzipping' results, but the ideas (mapping cylinder neighbourhoods, control data) were already known in the stratification literature.
transcription_corrections: 'Dans le cas de la notion de compatibilité stricte' should probably read 'Idem pour la notion de compatibilité stricte'.
The marginal note should read roughly: 'donc pour tout ε ∈ ]0,1[, ελT = ελ'T'' (not 'dans quel').
In the final paragraph the subspace is written Ṫ in the image, but it plays the role of Ẋ (the boundary) as on the next page.
'Item pour équivalence' is probably 'Idem pour ...' (word uncertain).
The parenthetical should read roughly '(Pour qu'il en soit ainsi, il faut que Y soit un sous-espace bord)', with the margin 'on dira aussi bien Y bord de X, ou X à bord...'.
